newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude called up on technical strength.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude called up on technical strength.

text.p: NYMEX crude was called to open higher Tuesday on technical strength while refined products were seen bolstered by position squaring ahead of weekly oil inventory data.
"The real strength is coming from crude after it was able to hold $24.00 yesterday," said Victor Yu, vice president with Refco Inc.
Crude was called 15 to 20 cents a barrel higher. Heating oil was called up 0.50 to 0.75 cent, with gasoline expected to open 0.25 to 0.50 cent a gallon higher.
This evening, American Petroleum Institute was expected to release its oil inventory data for the week ended Jan 31.
"Heating oil is up (on ACCESS) ahead of a possible fall in distillates," said a trader.
Preliminary estimates called for a two million barrel draw in distillate stocks, comprised of heating oil and diesel.
Monday, March heating oil ended 0.88 cent lower at 65.28 cents while March gasoline settled 0.09 cent higher at 68.35 cents. March crude finished unchanged at $24.15.
Distillate stocks stocks are expected to have declined due to higher demand fueled by colder weather when heating oil output is diminishing.
But the weather outlook is less supportive for heating oil.
Temperatures in the U.S. Northeast, which has the highest concentration of heating oil users, are expected to trend above above normal this week, said independent forecaster Weather Services Corp.
National Weather Service's six- to 10-day outlook for the Northeast calls for normal temperatures starting Feb 9.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
